children.value:
import numpy as np

# given input and target
x = np.array([1, 0, 1], dtype=float)
y = np.array([1], dtype=float)

# learning rate
lr = 0.001

# hidden layer weights, arranged as a (3 inputs x 2 hidden units) matrix
# column 0 -> hidden unit 1, column 1 -> hidden unit 2
Wh = np.array([
    [0.2, -0.3],   # weights coming from x1 (w11, w12)
    [0.4,  0.1],   # weights coming from x2 (w13, w14)
    [-0.5, 0.2]    # weights coming from x3 (w15, w16)
])
theta_h = np.array([-0.4, 0.2])   # theta1, theta2

# output layer weights, (2 hidden units x 1 output)
Wo = np.array([
    [-0.3],   # w21
    [-0.2]    # w22
])
theta_o = np.array([0.1])   # theta3

print("Wh =\n", Wh)
print("theta_h =", theta_h)
print("Wo =\n", Wo)
print("theta_o =", theta_o)

A few things worth pointing out:

Any weight connected to the first hidden unit ($w_{11}$, $w_{13}$, $w_{15}$, $\theta_1$) didn't change at all. That's because $Z_1$ was negative during the forward pass, so ReLU shut that unit off, and once a unit is off it stops passing gradient backward too.
The weights connected to the second hidden unit did move, since that unit was active.

With a learning rate this small (0.001), the updates are tiny after just one pass. It would take many iterations of this same process for the network to actually learn something useful, but this is exactly what happens on every single step of training.
